title: Tak to Kamphaeng Phet: 2-Day Heritage & Waterfall Trip | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night cross-province plan from Tak to Kamphaeng Phet, Thailand. Drive Highway 1 (about 1 hr), explore the UNESCO Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park (Wat Phra Kaeo, Wat Chang Rop), then Khlong Lan Waterfall — with real hours and fees.
keywords: Tak Kamphaeng Phet trip, Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park, Khlong Lan Waterfall, Kamphaeng Phet travel, Tak itinerary Thailand
h1:
Tak to Kamphaeng Phet
Historical Park + Waterfall, 2 Days 1 Night
intro: Tak and Kamphaeng Phet sit right next to each other — about an hour's drive apart — so it's easy to fold them into one trip. Day one is for walking the old city of Kamphaeng Phet, a UNESCO World Heritage town that's quieter and far less crowded than Sukhothai. Day two heads into the forest on the Khlong Lan side for the waterfalls. This is a detailed plan with real timings and entry fees, ready to use as is.

blocks.html: This route works well if you're already based in Tak, or just passing through on Highway 1 (Phahonyothin). It's about 60 km from Tak down to Kamphaeng Phet, roughly 1 hour, on good road the whole way. Driving yourself is by far the easiest option because the sights on the Kamphaeng Phet side are spread out — both the old city zone and the Khlong Lan forest, which is another 50 km or so beyond town.

items: Day 1 — Leave Tak, drive down to Kamphaeng Phet, walk the Historical Park (Wat Phra Kaeo, Wat Phra That, the Aranyik zone, Wat Chang Rop), and stay overnight in town.
Day 2 — Pay respects at Wat Phra Borommathat Nakhon Chum, then head into Khlong Lan to swim at Khlong Lan / Khlong Nam Lai waterfalls before looping back.
Getting around — A private car or rental is recommended. You can reach Kamphaeng Phet by bus, but the waterfall side needs a chartered vehicle.
Best time to go — The waterfalls are at their best in late rainy season and early cool season, around October to December, when the water runs full and clear.

blocks.text: Day 1 — The old city of Kamphaeng Phet

blocks.html: Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park is part of the same UNESCO World Heritage listing as Sukhothai and Si Satchanalai, but the mood here is clearly different. There are plenty of trees, lots of shade, and the ruins are built from reddish laterite. With far fewer visitors, you can wander and take photos without fighting anyone for an angle.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Tak city → Kamphaeng Phet old city

items.note: Drive south on Highway 1 for about 60 km, roughly 1 hour.

items.activity: Enter the walled-city zone — Wat Phra Kaeo, Wat Phra That
items.note: Open 08:30–16:30, entry 10 THB for Thais. Wat Phra Kaeo is the cluster of large stupas in the centre.

items.activity: Kamphaeng Phet National Museum — Buddha images and stone inscriptions
items.note: Next to the old city zone; it helps put the history in context before you walk on.
Made-to-order restaurants and noodle shops along Thesa Road, plenty to choose from.

items.activity: Aranyik zone (outside the walls) — Wat Chang Rop, Wat Phra Non
items.note: Entry to the outer zone is 50 THB per car. Wat Chang Rop, with its laterite elephant base surrounding a stupa, is the highlight.

items.activity: Stroll and shoot in the afternoon light — big shady trees throughout
items.note: The late-day light pairs nicely with the red laterite.

items.activity: Check in at your hotel in Kamphaeng Phet town
items.note: Hotels in town are affordable, starting around 500–900 THB/night.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The walled-city zone and the Aranyik zone have separate tickets, and driving into the outer zone adds a vehicle fee — keep some cash handy. Bring a hat and water too, since you'll be walking in the sun for a fair bit.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Nakhon Chum stupa + Khlong Lan Waterfall

blocks.html: On the second morning, stop to pay respects at Nakhon Chum, across the Ping River, then head into the Khlong Lan forest about 50 km from town. Khlong Lan Waterfall is a single tier over 100 metres high and roughly 40 metres wide, with a big pool to swim in. It's a short walk in from the car park.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Nakhon Chum → Khlong Lan National Park

items.activity: Wat Phra Borommathat Nakhon Chum — the gilded Burmese-style stupa
items.note: In Nakhon Chum subdistrict, just across the Ping River bridge.

items.activity: Drive into Khlong Lan district, about 50 km from town
items.note: The last stretch is a forest access road — drive slowly and watch the bends.

items.activity: Khlong Lan Waterfall — walk in for a swim
items.note: A tall single-tier fall with a large pool. Late rainy season is when the water is fullest and clearest.

items.activity: Lunch at the shops by the waterfall
items.note: Made-to-order food, som tam and grilled chicken, at typical tourist-spot prices.

items.activity: On to Khlong Nam Lai Waterfall (Pang Khwai) if you still have energy
items.note: A 9-tier waterfall with broad rock platforms — good for a relaxed soak.

items.activity: Pack up and loop back to Kamphaeng Phet town or up to Tak
items.note: Getting back into Tak takes about 1.5–2 hours, including the forest stretch.

blocks.text: Fees and opening hours to know

items: Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park — Open daily 08:30–16:30. Entry 10 THB for Thais, 30 THB for foreigners. The outer (Aranyik) zone charges a vehicle fee of 50 THB per car.
Khlong Lan National Park — Standard national-park entry fees apply. There are campgrounds and bungalows; book via nps.dnp.go.th.
Wat Phra Borommathat Nakhon Chum — Free to enter and open all day.
Key distances — Tak → Kamphaeng Phet ~60 km (~1 hr) · Kamphaeng Phet town → Khlong Lan ~50 km.

blocks.text: Can you do it in one day?

blocks.html: If you only have one day, picking one or the other works out better. Drive down from Tak, spend half a day at the Historical Park, then head back — or if you'd rather swim, go straight to Khlong Lan. Cramming both into a single day means rushing, since the waterfall sits in a different direction from the old city and you'd burn a lot of time driving back and forth.

items.name: History day
items.blurb: Spend the full day on the old city of Kamphaeng Phet, covering both the walled-city and outer zones at an unhurried pace.

items.name: Nature day
items.blurb: Head straight to Khlong Lan from the morning, swim at the waterfall for a good long while, and return in the evening.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: On the Khlong Lan side during the dry season (March–May), the waterfalls drop a lot, sometimes down to just a thin trickle. If you're coming specifically to swim, skip the dry months — late rainy season is far more worth it.

faq.q: How far is Tak from Kamphaeng Phet, and how long does it take?
faq.a: Not far — about 60 km along Highway 1, roughly 1 hour by car. The road is good the whole way, so self-driving is easy.

faq.q: What are the hours and entry fees for Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park?
faq.a: Open daily 08:30–16:30. Entry is 10 THB for Thais and 30 THB for foreigners. The Aranyik zone outside the walls adds a vehicle fee of 50 THB per car.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Khlong Lan Waterfall?
faq.a: Late rainy season into the cool season, around October to December, when the water is fullest and clearest. In the dry season from March to May the flow drops off sharply.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for this trip?
faq.a: 2 days and 1 night is about right — day one for the old city of Kamphaeng Phet, day two for Khlong Lan Waterfall. If you only have one day, pick one, since they're in different directions.

faq.q: Can I do this without my own car?
faq.a: For the old city of Kamphaeng Phet you can arrive by bus and get around town with local transport. But the Khlong Lan waterfall side is hard to reach by public transport — a chartered vehicle or your own car is much more convenient.
